title: U.S. House · New York's 6th Congressional District
area: Central Queens, entirely within New York City, including the neighborhoods of Flushing, Forest Hills, Rego Park, Elmhurst, East Elmhurst, Bayside, Auburndale, Glendale, Maspeth, Middle Village, Murray Hill, Kew Gardens Hills, and Woodside.

context.text: Meng defeated Chuck Park in a contested June 23, 2026 Democratic primary, 56.8% to 42.9% (18,971 to 14,335 votes).

Joseph Chou advanced from the Republican primary (canceled, unopposed) and the Conservative Party primary (canceled). Ballotpedia lists a "4 Our Immigrants Party" line for Chou as not making the ballot, so his general-election ballot lines are Republican and Conservative only.

Chou previously ran for this seat in 2024 (finishing third, with 1.6% of the vote on a third-party line, in a race Meng won with 60.5%) and for New York City Council District 20 in 2025 (finishing third with 4.4% of the vote).

summary.text: Grace Meng is the incumbent U.S. Representative for New York's 6th Congressional District, first elected in 2012. She is the first Asian American member of Congress from New York and serves on the House Committee on Appropriations, including its Commerce, Justice, Science, and National Security subcommittees.

background.text: Born in Queens, New York, in 1975; earned a bachelor's degree from the University of Michigan and a J.D. from the Benjamin Cardozo School of Law at Yeshiva University.
Worked as an attorney before entering elected office.
Served in the New York State Assembly representing District 22 from 2009 to 2013.
First Asian American member of Congress elected from New York; has served in the U.S. House since January 2013.

priorities.text: Has made opposition to a proposed citizenship question on the 2030 Census a recent focus, arguing an inaccurate count would misallocate congressional representation and federal funding.
priorities.quote: Every person living in our country must be counted, regardless of citizenship or immigration status. The Trump administration's proposal would erase millions of people from the census data used to distribute political representation.

priorities.text: Introduced legislation in response to a rise in ICE enforcement at immigration check-ins and courthouses, saying arrests have targeted people with no criminal record who are complying with legal requirements.
priorities.quote: Immigrants who are complying with the law have been detained and arrested while attending their scheduled check-ins. That's not enforcement, that's intimidation.

priorities.text: Has worked on bipartisan consumer-protection and hunger-relief legislation, including bills addressing SNAP benefit theft and mail access for incarcerated people.

positions.summary: Has introduced legislation to let immigrants complete ICE check-ins virtually rather than in person, in response to a sharp rise in arrests at routine check-ins and courthouses, and describes current ICE enforcement as targeting people with no criminal record.
positions.quote: ICE agents have been causing chaos in our communities for months. Immigrants who are complying with the law have been detained and arrested while attending their scheduled check-ins.

record.text: Introduced the Safe Check-Ins for Immigrants Act (H.R. 8381) on May 11, 2026, which would allow immigrants to complete required ICE check-ins via virtual platforms such as Zoom instead of appearing in person; the bill is supported by the New York Immigration Coalition, Asian American Federation, New Immigrant Community Empowerment, Adhikaar, and the Emerald Isle Immigration Center.

Introduced the bipartisan Ending Stolen SNAP Benefits Act (H.R. 9359) with Rep. Brian Fitzpatrick (R-PA), which would help states upgrade EBT card security to prevent "skimming" theft and allow the federal government to reissue stolen SNAP benefits.

Introduced the Stamps for Staying Connected Act (H.R. 10129) on September 16, 2026, which would authorize the Federal Bureau of Prisons to provide up to five additional stamps per week for general correspondence to incarcerated individuals who cannot afford postage.

Released a statement opposing the Trump administration's proposal to add a citizenship question to the 2030 Census, arguing it would undercount immigrant communities and misallocate congressional representation and federal funding.

Serves on the House Committee on Appropriations, including the Commerce, Justice, Science and Related Agencies and National Security/Department of State subcommittees, in the 119th Congress (2025–2026).

candidates.name: Joseph Chou
candidates.ballotNote: Advanced as the Republican and Conservative Party nominee after both primaries were canceled (unopposed)

summary.text: Joseph Chou is a naturalized U.S. citizen and small-business owner in Queens running as the Republican and Conservative Party nominee against incumbent Rep. Grace Meng. He previously ran for this same seat in 2024 (finishing third with 1.6% of the vote) and for New York City Council District 20 in 2025 (finishing third with 4.4%).

background.text: Describes himself as a naturalized citizen and small-business owner based in Queens.
Ran for New York's 6th Congressional District in 2024 on a minor-party line ("Truth Party"), finishing third with 1.6% of the vote.

Ran for New York City Council District 20 in the November 2025 general election on minor-party lines ("Asians United Party"/"F.A.F.O. Party"), finishing third behind incumbent Sandra Ung and Allen Wang with 4.4% of the vote.

priorities.text: Campaign lists four core priorities: economy and affordability, strengthening families, education, and immigration and border policy.
On the economy: campaign describes a "balanced tax policy that fosters growth" and lightens burdens for working families and small businesses, and fair student loan rates.
On immigration: says he supports "a fair, effective immigration system that honors the dignity of all who seek a life here," combined with enhanced inter-agency cooperation on criminal threats.
priorities.quote: A fair, effective immigration system that honors the dignity of all who seek a life here.

priorities.text: On education: campaign says it supports public, private, and alternative educational pathways, including vocational, arts, and science curricula, alongside parental empowerment in education decisions.

positions.summary: Campaign describes a "balanced tax policy that fosters growth" and lightens burdens for working families and small businesses, without proposing higher taxes on high earners or corporations.
Campaign supports funding for public, private, and alternative educational pathways alongside parental empowerment in education decisions.

Campaign frames immigration policy around fairness and human dignity combined with stronger inter-agency cooperation against criminal threats, without a specific stated position on ICE enforcement tactics.
